topics.label: Lecture framing and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience, introduces the lecture subject, and states what students should learn before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy as local cancer treatments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how surgery and radiotherapy can control tumors at specific sites, and why early detection and tumor location matter.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: efficacy, toxicity, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cytotoxic drugs damage cancer cells, their clinical benefits, and the toxicity and resistance that limit their use.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows how blocking hormone signaling can slow cancers that remain dependent on estrogen or androgens.

topics.label: Exploiting cell-cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how loss of checkpoint control can make cancer cells selectively vulnerable to radiation or oncolytic adenoviruses.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting PARP can make DNA damage lethal to cancer cells that lack BRCA-mediated repair.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic drivers with kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how oncogenic drivers can be identified and inhibited, and how kinase inhibitor selectivity and resistance limit this strategy.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how antibodies recognizing cell-surface targets can block cancer signaling, recruit immune activity, or deliver a cytotoxic drug.

topics.label: Immune surveillance, checkpoint inhibition, and tumour neoantigens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics connect evidence for immune recognition of cancer with T-cell reactivation and the role of neoantigens in treatment response.

topics.label: T-cell-engaging and CAR T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe ways to direct T-cell cytotoxic activity toward tumors, either by linking T cells to cancer cells or by engineering the T cells themselves.

topics.label: Challenges and personalised treatment strategies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers why cancer treatments do not work for everyone and how biomarkers and genome sequencing can help match therapies to patients.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends and the role of prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic assesses changes in cancer outcomes alongside prevention and screening measures that affect cancer incidence and detection.

topics.label: Future cancer treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider future directions and patient trade-offs, using childhood leukemia treatment success to illustrate the difficulty of trialling alternatives to effective existing regimens.
